annotations.text:
Fresh set, drawn from concept.md only.

Leading direction: the scoping task is ONE chat. Navigation follows the evidence-base task: Plan · Results · Sources · Share · History, with Results split into subtabs Baseline · Longlist · Shortlist. The longlist has List and Grid views; the shortlist tab shows the places with reasons before assessment and the assessed table, with a summary above it, after. There is no brief: Export bundles the assessed shortlist, the profiles, the baseline and what was searched. The longlist has a list view and a grid view; the shortlist is a state on its options, not a separate list. Screening is a pipeline stage, not a user step: it runs as each option's search finishes and shows as excluded options shown in place on the longlist. The baseline is built first and the run PAUSES: the user confirms the plan against it before any option is generated (owner ruling). Collapsed headers carry the takeaway, so the closed rail is the summary. One section opens at a time; the longlist, the grid and the profiles open wide, with the chat always on the left.

Below the brief and the sense-check: the option profile after a full run, the report task, and the tasks list. A full evidence search mints its own evidence-base task (7c, 7d); the scoping profile then reads from that report (7b). Design language follows the evidence-base report: one body size, grey for secondary text, states as words not chips, outputs as linear text.

Sample question: reducing the number of 16 to 24 year olds not in education, employment or training. All figures, quotes and sources are placeholders.

Rulings made visible:
· every option says what it is and which stated outcome it serves (4)
· baseline before longlist and the run pauses for plan confirmation (3)
· three depths: longlist carries metadata only (4); assessment = mini evidence search on the shortlist, user-triggered, labelled scoping pass, no full-text screening (5, 6); full evidence search per option confirms documents and mints the report (7c, 7d)
· do nothing is a reference wherever options appear (4, 5, 6)
· two kinds of constraint: checked at longlist, or after assessment with a labelled guess until then; guesses flag and sort, never drop (2, 4, 5, 6)
· every exclusion cites its constraint (4)
· thin evidence flags, never drops (4)
· add to shortlist / exclude / include again: adding keeps a place, never hides a screen finding (4, 5)
· the shortlist is a state on the longlist: the grid view shows coverage, each place proposed by Policy Atlas or added by you with one named reason (5)
· effect cell reports, never computes (6); a row opens the profile, no second layer in the table
· transferability shows its working, verdict capped (7)
· empty cells say why they are empty (6)
· Sources says what was searched; Export bundles the outputs (6b)

Two structural alternatives to the leading direction, both conversation-first.

A · Everything inline: living cards sit in the chat; superseded versions collapse to a stub. Trade-off: long scroll, the current state is never all in view.

B · Stage rail: each stage has its own chat and artifact. Trade-off: cleaner per stage, but breaks the single dialogue the owner asked for.
